records.Concise description: Blockstream's open-source Esplora explorer interface and HTTP API stack, publicly operated at Blockstream Explorer and commonly self-hosted with an Esplora-compatible backend.
records.Deeper researched summary: Esplora is an open-source block explorer frontend built around the Esplora HTTP API, commonly backed by esplora-electrs/electrs-style indexing. Blockstream operates the public blockstream.info explorer, while the software can also be self-hosted. MSC consolidates Esplora, Blockstream Explorer, and blockstream.info into one canonical profile because they are the same closely integrated explorer/API lineage rather than independent network entities.
records.Launch / history: Blockstream open-sourced Esplora as a Bitcoin explorer and API stack and continues to operate the hosted Blockstream Explorer.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It provides a durable, simple HTTP interface for transaction, block, address, and mempool data and is widely used as backend infrastructure by wallets and Bitcoin applications.
records.Verification basis: Blockstream's official repository, API documentation, and hosted explorer establish the consolidated product lineage.
Research notes / uncertainties: Explorer address views and labels are application/indexer state, not Bitcoin consensus state.
Do not create separate records for blockstream.info, Blockstream Explorer, and Esplora without a future schema reason.

records.Entity / project type: Bitcoin node crawler / network measurement service
records.Concise description: A Bitcoin P2P network crawler that measures reachable nodes, software versions, services, and inferred network distribution.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitnodes crawls Bitcoin peers by connecting to reachable nodes and recursively requesting peer addresses. Its methodology distinguishes reachable nodes that accept incoming connections from nodes that may exist but are unreachable to the crawler because of NAT, firewalls, outbound-only behavior, or other network conditions. Geographic and network-provider fields are inferred from observed endpoints and associated datasets, so node counts and location charts are measurements with visibility limits rather than exact population censuses.
records.Launch / history: Bitnodes has operated since the early 2010s. Its methodology remained actively documented and updated into late 2025, with live snapshots available in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is a primary ecosystem reference for observing the publicly reachable Bitcoin P2P network and for teaching why 'reachable node count' is not the same as 'all Bitcoin nodes.'
records.Verification basis: Current Bitnodes service and methodology were checked; methodology explicitly supports caveats around reachability and crawler visibility.
Research notes / uncertainties: Never present Bitnodes reachable-node counts as the exact total number of Bitcoin nodes.
Tor/onion visibility, NAT/firewalls, crawler vantage points, and address gossip affect coverage.
Geography is inferred from network endpoints and should not be treated as exact operator location.

records.Concise description: A database-free self-hosted Bitcoin explorer that reads blockchain and mempool data directly from Bitcoin Core RPC.
records.Deeper researched summary: BTC RPC Explorer is designed for node operators who want an explorer tied directly to their own Bitcoin Core instance instead of a hosted third party. It emphasizes RPC-driven block, transaction, address/script, mempool, fee, and node-information views without maintaining a separate primary application database for the canonical chain. Optional integrations can add richer address/history functionality. Its local-first model makes it a useful contrast with hosted/indexer-heavy explorers.
records.Launch / history: The project emerged in the late 2010s and remains maintained as a self-hosted explorer used by node distributions and individual operators.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It gives operators a private, node-backed inspection interface and helps separate raw node/RPC data from public explorer interpretations.
Important technical or cultural characte: Blocks, transactions, mempool and node views
records.Verification basis: Official repository and documentation establish the project's database-free Bitcoin Core RPC architecture and self-hosted role.
Research notes / uncertainties: Address history and richer views may depend on optional backends; do not imply Bitcoin Core RPC alone supplies every explorer feature.
Explorer presentation is not consensus state.

records.Concise description: A Lightning data and operations platform whose Space explorer exposes public network graph, node, channel, and analytics data alongside APIs and liquidity tooling.
records.Deeper researched summary: Amboss operates Space as a Lightning network explorer and analytics system, with node/channel search, network graph views, monitoring, and a GraphQL API. The broader Amboss platform also includes liquidity and other operational products such as Magma; MSC keeps these under one Amboss profile rather than splitting explorer, analytics, and liquidity product records. Amboss can observe public announcements and additional platform-collected data, but public graph capacity and advertised topology do not capture private channels or prove actual routing volume, profitability, or economic importance.
records.Launch / history: Amboss emerged in the early 2020s as a Lightning explorer and operator-data platform and remains actively documented and operated in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is a major Lightning observability layer for node operators and developers and a useful source for teaching the limits of public graph measurements.
Important technical or cultural characte: Node ownership verification by signed message
records.Verification basis: Current Amboss documentation was checked for Space explorer, API, node/channel data, and broader product consolidation.
Research notes / uncertainties: Public Lightning graph data excludes private channels and is not a complete measure of total liquidity or payment flow.
Node rankings, uptime, capacity, or connectivity metrics must not be presented as security or importance scores.
Magma remains part of the Amboss platform rather than a separate NETWORK profile.
